text:
A slap shot from Gustav Forsling at 4:55 of overtime, a chance that carried about a 5 percent shot of going in, decided a game Carolina controlled for most of the night. Florida won 1-0, but the Hurricanes created better looks (2.54 expected goals to 1.91) and deserved to win in 62 percent of simulated replays. Carter Verhaeghe picked up the assist on the winner.

The gap came from the middle of the game. Florida led the first period on chance quality, 0.47 to 0.22, then Carolina took over the second (1.41 to 0.99) and the third (0.80 to 0.32). Florida's edge came with the manpower even: 51 shot attempts to 37 overall, and 1.29 expected goals to 0.52 at even strength. The special teams offered no way out, since Florida went 0 for 6 on the power play and Carolina 0 for 7 in a game with 36 penalty minutes. Jackson Blake, Nikolaj Ehlers and Sebastian Aho all finished with team-best expected goals on the ice, and Aho put four shots on net.

The difference was Jacob Markstrom. Carolina put 20 shots on him, and he stopped all of them, saving about 2.54 goals more than an average goalie would have against that workload. Brandon Bussi was good too, stopping 14 of 15 and finishing 0.91 goals above expected, but one clean shot from the point was all it took. Markstrom took second star behind Forsling, though the numbers say he was the reason the game reached overtime at all.
